The failing test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected` in the `FastDateFormat_PrinterTest` class from the `org.apache.commons.lang3.time` package is testing the behavior of date formatting with time zones in the `FastDateFormat` class. The test creates a `Calendar` instance with a specific time zone and then attempts to format the time using the `FastDateFormat` class.

The bug report describes that the `FastDateFormat` class's "z" pattern does not respect the timezone of `Calendar` instances passed to the `format` method. This behavior contradicts the expected behavior where the time zone should be respected when formatting the time.

Looking at the implementation of the `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String pattern)` method, it retrieves an instance of `FastDateFormat` from a cache without taking the time zone into account. This could lead to the reported issue where the time zone of the `Calendar` instance is not considered during formatting.

To address this bug, the `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String pattern)` method needs to be updated to take into account the time zone when formatting the time.

Next, I will suggest the method to be fixed.
### Diagnosis

The issue stems from the `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String pattern)` method in the `org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateFormat` class. This method retrieves a `FastDateFormat` instance from a cache without considering the time zone when formatting the time. As a result, when the `format` method is called on the obtained `FastDateFormat` instance with a `Calendar` object with a specific time zone, the timezone information is not respected during formatting, leading to the observed bug.

### Suggested Fix
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateFormat.getInstance(String)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
